items.title: Here's what happened in crypto today
items.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Switzerland clears 57 jurisdictions for crypto tax data sharing
items.summary: The move paves the way for Switzerland to exchange crypto tax data with foreign authorities starting in 2028 as part of a global effort to combat tax evasion.

items.title: Braiins warns of Bitcoin mining attacks affecting over 1,000 sites
items.summary: Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins warned that attackers are exploiting unsecured connections to hijack miners' computing power and potentially steal rewards.

items.title: Why ECB collateral eligibility could boost demand for tokenized bonds
items.summary: Past ECB decisions offer clues to the value of using bonds as collateral, while US derivatives exchanges face a different calculation over their Bitcoin holdings.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation backs Keccak-256 to counter quantum, AI threats
items.summary: Ethlabs co-founder Julian Ma told Cointelegraph that AI poses a more immediate threat as Ethereum prepares for one of its biggest security overhauls since the Merge.

items.title: US inflation rises to 3.8% ahead of December Fed meeting, clouding crypto outlook
items.summary: US core inflation rose more than expected in October as markets anticipate a December interest rate hike, which could slow a crypto market recovery.

items.title: China's Google Just Released Its Fast New AI Model for Free
items.summary: Baidu has released the weights of its new high-speed reasoning model, giving developers a commercially usable alternative to proprietary AI services from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic

items.title: What Happened to Alice Huang, the Woman at the Center of Nvidia's Scandal?
items.summary: U.S. intelligence found no evidence that Beijing directed Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia's CEO, but the former Megaspeed executive still faces entry bans and scrutiny of business ties.

items.title: The 1Password Breach Didn't Touch Your Vault. The Phishing Emails Might
items.summary: An attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account to reach 1Password's backend and copy customer names and emails, but the company says vault contents, encryption keys and your Secret Key were never exposed.

items.title: Another Bitcoin Mining Firm Flags 'Hashrate Hijacking' Attacks That Reroute Rewards
items.summary: Braiins says an attacker exploited the unencrypted Stratum V1 protocol and internet route hijacking to impersonate mining pools, striking over 1,000 sites in a single second.

items.title: What Is Artex? The AI Hacking Tool Linked to the US Spy Agency Breach
items.summary: Microsoft says state-backed hackers and cybercriminals are using Artex to automate attacks with AI agents, exploiting familiar security flaws at speeds that leave defenders little time to respond or recover.

items.title: Nvidia to Pay $290 Million to Settle Long-Running Crypto Mining Revenue Lawsuit
items.summary: The proposed cash settlement would resolve a shareholder suit alleging the chipmaker hid how much of its 2017-2018 gaming revenue came from crypto miners.

items.title: Sens. Warren, Van Hollen lead push to scrap SEC's Regulation Crypto and innovation exemption
items.summary: Sens. Warren and Van Hollen sent two letters to SEC Chair Atkins demanding he rescind the innovation exemption and Regulation Crypto.

items.title: Bitcoin miners hit by hashrate hijacking attack exploiting unencrypted connections
items.summary: Braiins warns that an attacker is redirecting miners' compute power to steal bitcoin mining rewards.

items.title: Fidelity files for spot Chainlink ETF with planned Nasdaq listing
items.summary: Fidelity has filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund.

items.title: Justice Department takes aim at billions in crypto fraud proceeds in historic 'largest ever crackdown'
items.summary: Following President Trump's directive to crack down on fraud, the Justice Department announced what it called its "largest-ever crackdown."

items.title: Nvidia agrees to $290 million settlement over crypto mining disclosures amid Jensen Huang turmoil
items.summary: Nvidia agreed to a $290M settlement over claims it misled investors about crypto mining demand driving 2017-18 gaming GPU sales.
